Ordinary kriging

Source: R/krg.R
okrge.Rd

Predicts the values at new locations at by ordinary kriging: the best linear unbiased predictor under a variogram model with an unknown constant mean (Cressie 1993, sec. 3.2), with its kriging variance. The variogram is vgm, a list such as vgfit() returns; without it, an exponential model is fitted by weighted least squares to the 15-bin vgemp() semivariogram with the weights np / h^2 of Cressie (1985), which is fast but rougher than vgfit().

Usage

okrge(x, y = NULL, v, at, vgm = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

The points: x and y numeric vectors of equal length; or x a matrix or data frame with columns named x and y (or X and Y, as sf::st_coordinates() names them, or lon and lat with lonlat = TRUE) and y NULL; or x an sf or sfc object of POINT geometries, whose coordinate reference system must agree with lonlat. An unnamed two-column matrix is read as x then y; other columns are never taken by position. Vectors given separately (x, y, and w or t where a function takes them) are matched by name when every one is named and no name repeats, as elsewhere in the package; otherwise by position. No missing or infinite values.

v

The values: finite numbers, one per point.

at

The prediction locations: a matrix or data frame of two coordinate columns, as x.

vgm

NULL, or a list with model ("exponential", "spherical" or "gaussian"), nugget, psill (from 0) and range (positive).

Value

A data frame with one row per prediction location: pred and var (the kriging variance, at least 0).

References

Cressie, N. (1985). Fitting variogram models by weighted least squares. Mathematical Geology, 17(5), 563-586. doi:10.1007/BF01032109

Cressie, N. (1993). Statistics for Spatial Data, revised edition. Wiley, New York. doi:10.1002/9781119115151

See also

Other geostatistics: bkrig(), crsof(), krigcv(), lfspec(), sglmx(), smixm(), spobj(), spsamp(), spxy(), trsurf(), vgemp(), vgfit()

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = runif(60), y = runif(60))
v <- sin(3 * p[, 1]) + rnorm(60, sd = 0.1)
okrge(p, v = v, at = cbind(0.5, 0.5))
#>      pred        var
#> 1 1.06704 0.01030984
okrge(p, v = v, at = cbind(0.5, 0.5),
      vgm = list(model = "exponential", nugget = 0.01, psill = 0.3,
                 range = 0.4))
#>       pred        var
#> 1 1.062215 0.04918238
